rubric.why: Identifies the information that is protected as secret.
rubric.description: States that a trade secret is confidential business information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as confidential information or business information.

rubric.why: States the value of the information or that it is withheld from others.
rubric.description: Explains that it provides a competitive advantage or is kept secret.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning its competitive advantage or that it is kept secret.

modelAnswer: A trade secret is confidential business information that gives a business an advantage over its competitors.
It is kept secret from competitors and the public.

items.followUp: Name one wired and one wireless transmission medium.

rubric.why: States the basic role of a transmission medium.
rubric.description: Says that the medium carries or transmits data signals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its data-carrying function.

rubric.why: Identifies the endpoints between which data is transferred.
rubric.description: States that the medium carries data from the sender to the receiver, or equivalent endpoints.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the sending and receiving endpoints.

modelAnswer: A transmission medium is the path or channel that carries data signals.
It transfers data from the sender to the receiver.

items.followUp: How many bits are in an IPv4 address, and how is it commonly written?

rubric.why: Gives the defining length of an IPv4 address.
rubric.description: States that an IPv4 address is 32 bits long.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct address length.

rubric.description: States that an IPv4 address is divided into four parts and commonly written in dotted-decimal form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its four-part or dotted-decimal representation.

modelAnswer: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit address used to identify a device on a network.
It is divided into four 8-bit parts and commonly written in dotted-decimal form, for example, 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: What protocol is commonly used to receive email from a mail server?

rubric.why: Identifies SMTP's main role in email communication.
rubric.description: States that SMTP is used to send outgoing email.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its email-sending function.

rubric.why: Explains where or between which systems SMTP transfers email.
rubric.description: States that SMTP transfers outgoing email to a mail server or between mail servers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning transfer to a mail server or between mail servers.

modelAnswer: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is used to send outgoing email.
It transfers email from a sender's device to a mail server and between mail servers.
